nice_guideline_used: NICE CG114 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management); NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease in adults: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg as tolerated
medications.purpose: RAAS blockade to reduce intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG114 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for proteinuric CKD (ACR ≥30 mg/mmol) to lower proteinuria and slow progression

medications.dose: 1 mg/kg body weight per day (max 80 mg) oral in the morning for 4–6 months, then taper
medications.duration: Induction 4–6 months, then taper based on response
medications.purpose: Induction immunosuppression for primary FSGS to achieve remission of proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: UK Renal Association consensus aligns with NICE general steroid use recommendations for glomerular diseases; steroids are first‑line disease‑modifying therapy for primary FSGS

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²; ACE‑I dosing may need adjustment if eGFR <30 (per NICE NG203).
Serum potassium not provided – assumed ≤5.5 mmol/L; hyperkalaemia would contraindicate ACE‑I (per NICE CG114).
Pregnancy status unknown – ACE‑I and high‑dose steroids are contraindicated in pregnancy; must be confirmed before prescribing.
Current medication list not provided – cannot assess drug‑drug interactions (e.g., potassium‑sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, other RAAS blockers).
Allergy status to ACE‑I or steroids not provided – must be verified.
Blood pressure and proteinuria levels not provided – target BP <130/80 mm Hg and proteinuria monitoring per NICE CG114.
treatment_summary: Start ACE‑I (ramipril) with dose titration and oral prednisone induction therapy, pending confirmation of renal function, potassium, pregnancy status and medication review. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, blood pressure, glucose and proteinuria according to NICE CG114 and NG203.
